boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Buckland Mills record (October 19, 1863) in the Bristoe Campaign [October-November 1863]. Humphreys places the action on October 20; the frozen date is retained. Campaign-wide marches, captures, returns and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads Divisions; the live field reads zero. Stuart gives Kilpatrick ten regiments of cavalry and six guns. Humphreys says the whole Confederate cavalry was engaged, with 6,867 enlisted men present on its October 20 return, against Kilpatrick's 3,500 on September 30.
claims.rationale: Returns and a regiment count differ in date and scope; none is adopted. Live zeros are not measured absence.

claims.value: The frozen and live results read Confederate victory. NPS says the Union cavalry was lured into an ambush and routed; Stuart calls the rout the most complete any cavalry suffered in the war. Stuart's dispatch dated October 20 places the fight 'yesterday', while Humphreys narrates it on the 20th.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. The date conflict is recorded, not resolved; the frozen October 19 is retained.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 230 total; the live field reads zero. Humphreys, citing the Medical and Surgical History, gives 20 killed, 60 wounded and 100 missing in Kilpatrick's division and 10 killed and 40 wounded in Stuart's cavalry, which sum to 230 (a computation here). Stuart reported about 200 prisoners and about 30 casualties in his dispatch and about 250 prisoners in his later report.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap.

open_questions: Kilpatrick's, Custer's, Davies's and Fitzhugh Lee's reports remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. Humphreys is an interested history by the Army of the Potomac's chief of staff in 1863–64, per his publisher's list. Stuart's, A. P. Hill's and Lee's reports, printed in Official Records Series I, Volume XXIX, Part 1, are separate families of interested Confederate commanders' accounts; the volume is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
